question: Who among the following was the chairman of Planning Commission when the First Five Year plan was started?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was the **Chairman of the Planning Commission** when the First Five-Year Plan was launched in India.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was implemented from **1951 to 1956** and focused on agricultural development and self-sufficiency in food production.
 
• The Planning Commission was established in **1950** with the primary objective of formulating and guiding economic plans for India.
 
• As the first Prime Minister of India, Nehru played a pivotal role in shaping the country's economic and social policies during the early years of independence.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was inspired by the Harrod-Domar Model and emphasized **community development projects**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planning Commission of India**:

 
 
• It was a government body established in **March 1950** by a resolution of the Government of India.
 
• The primary role of the Planning Commission was to formulate five-year plans and allocate resources effectively.
 
• It was dissolved in **2014** and replaced by the **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India).
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans**:
 
 
• India adopted the concept of Five-Year Plans from the Soviet Union to achieve planned economic development.
 
• The First Plan focused on **agriculture, irrigation, and energy**, aiming to improve food production and rural development.
 
• The success of the First Plan laid the foundation for future economic planning in India.
 
 
 
• **Harrod-Domar Model**:
 
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was based on this economic model, which emphasizes the relationship between savings, investment, and economic growth.
 
• It suggested that higher savings and investment levels are crucial for sustained economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru's Vision**:
 
 
• Nehru emphasized industrialization, scientific temper, and self-reliance as essential components of India's progress.
 
• His leadership during the formative years of India's economy ensured a strong foundation for future development.
